Face off: Are classic games worth playing today?

I kind of agree with Livingston's take on the subject, but I'd also add the following:

Some of the older games that I like - games like Raptor: Call of the Shadows or OverKill - are actually a lot simpler than some of the more modern games.

It's straightforward "go here, blow shit up, get upgrades, blow more shit up" instead of "go here, pull this lever, grab that device, take it to Old Man Jenkins in the Bakhov Beyond, find out what it is, go get the things he needs to fix it, then you get to go blow shit up".

And sometimes, all you want is to just blow shit up without any complicated rigamarole.

I agree. Sometimes it's very refreshing to go back and play older video games where the objectives are simple and the methods to complete the objectives are just as simple.

I wouldn't go as far to say that all new games coming out are bad. No doubt there are games where the cut scenes are overdone and having to complete a twenty minute tutorial level feels more like a chore than fun.

I do like being able to, say, play an old FPS like Doom or Duke 3D where the goal is to simply flip a switch to complete a level. I also miss being able to pick up games and simply figure out how to play them by playing them. Maybe it's nostalgia speaking but I wish more games like that were made.

It depends. Most games from the NES/SNES generation are pretty great and still exceedingly playable, but a lot of the early 3D stuff is hot garbage. Graphics that look like puke, janky controls, and unworkable cameras. Those games were amazing then, but playing a lot of them now I'm like, "How the hell did we ever put up with this shit?"

I rarely buy new games now. The last game I bought was Last of Us.

There's such a wealth of Abandonia that I won't be able to exhaust it before I die! I'm currently running through the Eye of The Beholder series with the occasional spree on classic Legend of Zelda games on my softmodded Wii.
